The regression is that in Vite 8 the `import.meta.glob` pattern using extglobs no longer matches, so no page components are detected, `dynamicImports` disappears from the manifest, and no code splitting happens [4][5].   "!./{stories,types,Common,lib,const,admin-ui}/*.tsx",
```ts
  "!./*/*.{spec,test,stories}.tsx",
]) as Record<string, () => Promise<IdMap<any>>>;
```

Note that `**` matches any nesting depth, so use `./*/*.tsx` if you need exactly one level deep like `category/name.tsx` [1][2]. Extglob support is being tracked separately at https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/21947 [3].

That's why your logs come out as `[1] => [2] => [4] => [3]` instead of the expected `[1] => [2] => [3] => [4]` under UMD, while dev mode and ES-format production builds are correct [2]. The underlying cause is tracked upstream in rollup/rollup#4166 [3]. The execution order is reportedly preserved in Vite 8+ and Rolldown [4].

answer: Setting `server.hmr: false` disables HMR, but the WebSocket itself cannot be turned off because it's used for features other than HMR [1][4]. If your goal is to stop the auto page refresh, that's a separate question the maintainer asked about [4]. There is no supported way to disable both the WebSocket and HMR [1][5]. A user-shared workaround is to override the web content in Chrome DevTools and make `setupWebSocket` return `null` [3].

The fix is to upgrade `@braintree/sanitize-url` to a newer version: 7.1.2 works, and the issue is confirmed fixed with 8.0.11 [2][3][4]. The root cause is that 7.1.1 reassigns `exports.sanitizeUrl` after a `void 0` initialization, which breaks the CJS analysis, whereas 7.1.2 exports it directly [4]. As Artur- notes, "the workaround for Mermaid today is trivial - use the latest version of sanitize-url" [1]. The Vite-side fix was skipped in favor of the dependency upgrade [5].

```json
"@braintree/sanitize-url": "^7.1.2"
```
